summary: A high-level introduction to the capabilities of SCTP, aimed at potential users. It is informational.

eli5.summary: SCTP is a way to send data. This is the friendly first tour of what it can do.

questions: how is sctp different from tcp
subtitle: A reliable message-oriented protocol with multiple streams and multi-homing support.

tldr.problem: Traditional transport protocols like TCP guarantee ordered delivery but can't efficiently handle applications that don't need strict ordering across all data, such as telephony signaling where different resources can be handled independently.
tldr.mechanism: SCTP provides reliable, ordered delivery while allowing data to be partitioned into independent streams. It also supports multi-homing, where a single connection can use multiple IP addresses for redundancy.
tldr.outcome: SCTP proved valuable for signaling protocols but never achieved widespread adoption as a general-purpose replacement for TCP. It remains an Internet Standard and is used in specific telecommunications applications.

today: RFC 3286 provides an introduction to SCTP. The full specification is RFC 2960, which defines SCTP as an Internet Standard. SCTP remains an Internet Standard and has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: What SCTP Is
sections.content: The Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) is an IP transport protocol that sits alongside TCP and UDP. Like TCP, it guarantees reliable, ordered delivery of data and maintains a session-like connection between two endpoints. The difference is that SCTP is message-oriented, meaning it preserves message boundaries instead of treating data as a stream of bytes.
sections.eli5: SCTP is a way to send messages reliably, like TCP, but it keeps each message separate instead of mixing them all together.

sections.title: Multi-Streaming: Independent Message Lanes
sections.content:
SCTP's defining feature is multi-streaming. A single SCTP connection can split data into multiple independent streams, each with its own sequence numbers. If a message is lost in one stream, the receiver can still deliver messages from other streams while waiting for retransmission in the affected stream. TCP, by contrast, must hold up delivery of all data until the lost message arrives.

This is particularly useful in telephony signaling, where different calls or resources can be handled independently. A lost message affecting call A should not delay the delivery of messages for call B.
sections.eli5: If one mail lane has a delay, the other lanes don't have to wait. Each lane delivers its packages independently.

sections.title: Multi-Homing: Backup Addresses
sections.content:
SCTP supports multi-homing, allowing a single endpoint to be reachable through multiple IP addresses. Each endpoint exchanges its address list during connection setup. One address is designated as the primary address used for normal data transmission, while alternate addresses serve as backups in case of network failure.

If the primary address becomes unreachable, SCTP automatically switches to an alternate address. The protocol sends periodic heartbeat messages to inactive addresses to detect when they become reachable again. This improves reliability in networks with redundant connectivity.
sections.eli5: The house has multiple mailboxes on different streets. If one gets blocked, the mailman can deliver through another one.

sections.title: Connection Setup and Shutdown
sections.content:
SCTP uses a four-message handshake to establish a connection, similar to TCP. During this exchange, both endpoints negotiate the number of streams and exchange address lists. The protocol includes a cookie mechanism to defend against denial-of-service attacks: the server creates an opaque cookie containing connection state, so the server need not allocate memory until the client proves it received the cookie and sent it back.

Shutdown uses a three-message sequence where each endpoint confirms receipt of the other's data before the connection closes. This ensures no data is lost.
sections.eli5: Before using the connection, both sides shake hands and exchange information. When done, they politely confirm all messages arrived before closing.

sections.title: Data Flow, Error Recovery and Security
sections.content:
SCTP follows TCP's selective acknowledgment method: the receiver acknowledges not just the highest received sequence number but also any gaps, allowing the sender to retransmit only the missing pieces. Flow and congestion control mirror TCP, with slow start, congestion avoidance, and fast retransmit.

The protocol uses a 32-bit verification tag to prevent insertion of old or false messages. SCTP itself does not define new security protocols but is designed to work with IPSec for strong security. The message format allows for extensions with new chunk types, provided they are standardized through the IETF.
sections.eli5: The sender keeps track of what was received. If something is missing, it gets sent again. The protocol includes a secret code to make sure messages are real.
